otp_summary: The LPDDR5 SDRAM die does not expose a normative user OTP / fuse array at the bus interface. JESD209-5 standardizes a volatile DRAM array plus a mode-register space that must be re-programmed after each power cycle. Unlike DDR3 DIMMs, mobile LPDDR5 is soldered directly to the board and there is no separate I2C Serial Presence Detect (SPD) EEPROM; instead, the device exposes read-only device-information mode registers (manufacturer ID, revision/stepping, density / I/O width / type, and feature/support flags) that the controller reads via Mode Register Read (MRR) at boot. The DRAM die may carry vendor-internal trim/repair fuses, but these are not exposed at the bus interface and are not normative in JESD209-5.

device_info_mode_registers_summary.access: Read via Mode Register Read (MRR) over the 7-bit CA bus; returns OP[7:0] on DQ.

key_fields.name: Manufacturer ID
key_fields.description: JEP106 vendor identifier of the LPDDR5 die.

key_fields.name: Density / I/O width / type
key_fields.description: Per-channel density, x16 organization, and LPDDR5 device-type identification.

key_fields.name: Feature / support flags
key_fields.description: Supported features: bank modes (BG/16B/8B), WCK ratios, link-ECC support, RFM support, DVFS / FSP capabilities, deep-sleep support.

key_fields.name: Refresh / temperature status
key_fields.description: Temperature range and refresh-rate status (MR4-class), read by the controller to adapt refresh.

factory_programmed_dram_die_metadata: The DRAM die may carry vendor-internal trim fuses, redundancy-repair fuses, and stepping ID, but these are not exposed at the bus interface and are not normative in JESD209-5.
permanent_state_after_power_off: DRAM array contents are volatile (lost on supply removal). Mode registers are also volatile and must be re-programmed on every power-up / after reset and after deep-sleep exit. There is no non-volatile SPD EEPROM on a soldered LPDDR5 device; the read-only device-info mode registers serve as the controller's in-band identification path.
notes: From the controller's perspective, the read-only device-information mode registers (manufacturer/revision/density/feature flags) are the canonical identification fingerprint of an LPDDR5 device, read in-band via MRR — replacing the separate I2C SPD EEPROM used on DDR3 DIMMs. JESD209-5 is the definitive document for the mode-register layout; this layer summarizes the key read-only fields a host controller must parse.
